record.dct_title_s: Aerial Imagery for Dunn County, WI 2023
dct_description_sm: This project established digital, 4-band orthoimagery for Dunn County, Wisconsin as part of the Wisconsin Regional Orthoimagery Consortium (WROC). Ayres Associates provided Dunn County, Wisconsin with digital, 4-band orthoimagery services in 2023 as part of WROC. The aerial imagery was collected on April 18th and 26nd using a Microsoft Vexcel UltraCam Eagle M3 sensor mounted in a fixed-wing aircraft. Aerial imagery was collected to support 0.5 foot ground sample distance (GSD) orthoimagery to meet ASPRS Class II horizontal accuracy specifications at 1 inch = 100 feet map scale. The 6-inch pixel orthoimagery was produced to meet or exceed a horizontal accuracy of 1.4 feet RMSE according to ASPRS Positional Accuracy Standards for Digital Geospatial Data. Resultant orthoimagery was rectified to a DEM created from LiDAR data acquired in 2019. Orthoimagery was delivered in PLSS section GeoTiff and MrSID tiles and a project wide MrSID mosaic. The orthoimagery was delivered according to a section tile schematic. The project area covers approximately 864 square miles. Supplemental Information: The Wisconsin Regional Orthoimagery Consortium (WROC) is a multi-entity group of county members and partners led by regional planning commissions (RPCs) and WROC representatives from Ayres Associates. The goal of the consortium is to build and sustain a multi-participant program to acquire digital orthoimagery and elevation data throughout Wisconsin. Orthoimagery was collected for Dunn County in 2023 to provide consistent deliverable products and accuracy standards for each of the participating entities. Note to users: The spring of 2023 was unusually wet in the region, therefore these images show more flooding in Dunn County than is expected in a typical year.

dct_description_sm: This raster dataset is a detailed (1-acre minimum), hierarchically organized vegetation cover map produced by computer classification of combined two-season pairs of early-1990s Landsat 4/5 Thematic Mapper (TM) satellite imagery, as part of the Upper Midwest Gap Analysis Program (UMGAP)(http://www.umesc.usgs.gov/umgaphome.html) of the U.S. Geological Survey. Units of analysis were Minnesota Ecological Classification System (ECS)(http://www.dnr.state.mn.us/ecs/index.html) subsections subdivided by TM scenes. GAP typology and classification protocols are closely comparable across Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan.
